label: I q.80 a.1 co. and ad 3 — A natural form is followed by inclination
locator: I q.80 a.1 co. and ad 3
interpretation: Aquinas contrasts the natural inclination attached to a thing’s form with an animal’s appetite for what it apprehends. A power’s natural inclination to its fitting activity is distinct from the animal’s appetite for something fitting to it as an animal.
attribution: The passage states that a natural form is followed by a natural inclination and that each power of the soul, considered as a nature, has its own natural inclination to a fitting object, which is the premise.
